\section{Scope and unresolved extensions}
\label{sec:limits}

The nonlinear theorems concern the exact $\SU$ geometry of a single star, but
the two rational spectra concern the linearization about the identity on one
finite open block.  Five extensions are not supplied here.

First, equation~\eqref{eq:det-transfer} requires a uniform centered-coordinate
remainder before it can transfer the Gaussian tail to an interacting
nonlinear measure.  Second, the exact spectrum has not been proved uniform in
block size or for periodic boundary conditions.  Third, the spill calculation
is infinitesimal; a finite nonlinear coordinated link transformation with a
controlled Jacobian remains to be built.  Fourth, nonzero pre-existing
external curvature introduces cross terms that can either help or hurt a
repair and must be treated probabilistically.  Fifth, no iteration across
renormalization scales is established.

These omissions are logically upstream of any continuum or spectral claim.
The present results neither construct four-dimensional Yang--Mills theory nor
prove clustering, Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction, or a mass gap.  Their
role in such a program is diagnostic: they identify a gauge-invariant local
badness variable, compute its correct dependent Gaussian reference law, and
show that an apparently local repair in that variable is not microscopically
external-flat.

A high-value next theorem would combine several neighboring stars so that
their spill fields cancel.  Algebraically, this replaces one constraint
$R_\ell x=y$ by a polymer constraint and asks how the minimum-spill spectrum
scales with the polymer boundary.  A boundary rather than volume bound would
turn the present obstruction into a constructive design principle.
